summary: Backend-only RETEST of the two iteration_1 defects. Extended the pytest suite to 21 tests (/app/backend/tests/backend_test.py + new /app/backend/tests/test_backfill_drift.py); 20/21 pass. FIX #1 VERIFIED: POST /api/actions/send and POST /api/withdrawals with an Idempotency-Key that fails validation now return 400 'Solde insuffisant', the PROCESSING idempotency_records doc is deleted (verified in Mongo), and retrying the SAME key with a corrected valid amount returns 200 {ok:true} debiting exactly once (no 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS). Idempotency semantics remain correct: same key + same valid body replays the same tx_id/wd_id with no second debit and a single transaction + single ledger entry; same key + different body still returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (send + withdrawals); keys are scoped per user. FIX #2 PARTIALLY VERIFIED: POST /api/admin/ledger/backfill works — on a deliberately drifted account it appends a balanced 'Migration' opening entry (acct_cash_<uid> +300 / acct_sys_issuance -300, category='Migration'), after which /api/admin/ledger/integrity returns balanced=true, cache_mismatches==[] and /api/admin/financial-health returns ledger_balanced=true, jcc_supply_reconciled=true, severity=INFO; a 2nd immediate call reports accounts_backfilled=0. Admin-only enforcement OK: backfill/financial-health/integrity all 403 for non-admin and 401 unauthenticated. No regression: send WITHOUT an Idempotency-Key debits once, transaction persisted, cache == derived ledger balance, per_asset_sum JCC == 0, coffre move still posts a balanced ledger entry. ONE NEW DEFECT: backfill can only ever fix an account once (static idempotency_key 'backfill:<account>'), so a later drift on the same account is silently NOT corrected while the endpoint still reports accounts_backfilled=1 (false success).

minor.issue: ledger_post is called with a STATIC idempotency_key f'backfill:{acct}'. Once an account has been backfilled, any future cache/ledger drift on the same account can never be migrated: ledger_post returns the existing entry, no compensating posting is written, yet fixed++ still runs so the response reports accounts_backfilled=1 while /api/admin/ledger/integrity still lists the mismatch (reproduced: cached 450 vs derived 300). Fix: make the key drift-specific (e.g. f'backfill:{acct}:{diff}:{timestamp}' or hash of the diff) and only increment the counter when an entry was actually inserted.

Still limited to db.users.find().limit(50) and still ignores coffres.amount_cc vs acct_coffre_* derived balances, so cache drift is invisible beyond 50 users / for coffres (backfill itself does iterate coffres). Paginate and add coffre accounts to cache_mismatches.
Still no IBAN format validation in WithdrawRequest (any string accepted).
Still no Idempotency-Key support and still mutates coffres.amount_cc/users.balance_cc before ledger_post; a duplicated client call moves funds twice.

No TTL index on idempotency_records.created_at. idem_fail only covers exceptions inside the handler; a hard process crash between idem_begin and idem_finish still leaves a permanent PROCESSING record (no expiry path).

action_items: Make /api/admin/ledger/backfill re-runnable: derive the ledger_post idempotency key from the actual diff (or drop it and count only real insertions) so recurring drift can be corrected and accounts_backfilled is truthful.
Extend /api/admin/ledger/integrity to all users (pagination) and to coffre accounts.
Add a TTL index on idempotency_records.created_at as a safety net for crash-orphaned PROCESSING records.

Confirm the production data reset was intentional: all 3 real users (kimoune2025@gmail.com, djsayd972@gmail.com, factorymaker.records@gmail.com) now have balance_cc=0, all 12 coffres amount_cc=0 and ledger_entries is empty. jcc_supply_reconciled=true is therefore currently trivial (0 == 0) — the reconciliation was proven on synthetic drift, not on real legacy balances.
critical_code_review_comments: ledger_backfill(): 'fixed' is incremented even when ledger_post short-circuits on the existing idempotency_key -> misleading response and hidden unreconciled drift.

idem_fail() deletes only {state:'PROCESSING'} which is correct, but the delete is best-effort inside the except block; if idem_fail itself raises (DB down) the key stays poisoned — wrap in try/except and rely on a TTL index.
get_or_seed_card(): duplicated db.cards.find_one call (lines 216-217) is still dead code.
ledger_integrity() and financial_health() still duplicate the same per-asset Python aggregation loop over ALL ledger entries; extract a shared Mongo $unwind/$group aggregation.
server.py is 1207 lines - split into routers (auth, wallet, ledger, admin, agents, card).

All test users, sessions, transactions, withdrawals, coffres, idempotency records, ledger entries and backfill migration entries deleted at teardown (verified: 0 TEST_* docs remain, idempotency_records=0, no PROCESSING records).
test_credentials: /app/memory/test_credentials.md is still an empty template (no credentials). Auth is Emergent Google; tests seed users+sessions directly in MongoDB (conftest._mk_user).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -n 0 -v (use -n 0; xdist races on shared balances/global integrity assertions). Both iteration_1 defects are fixed. The single remaining failure is tests/test_backfill_drift.py::test_backfill_cannot_fix_a_second_drift_on_same_account (static backfill idempotency key). NOTE: the live DB is currently empty of balances/ledger entries, so global integrity/health assertions pass trivially; if real balances are re-seeded, re-run TestAdminIntegrity first (it calls backfill before asserting). Frontend intentionally not tested.
rca_of_the_issue: Backfill re-drift bug: ledger_backfill() passes idempotency_key=f'backfill:{account}' to ledger_post(), which returns the pre-existing entry_id whenever that key is found and writes nothing. The first migration therefore permanently consumes the key for that account; a subsequent cache/ledger divergence produces diff != 0, enters the branch, no-ops in ledger_post, but still increments 'fixed', so the endpoint reports a successful backfill while /api/admin/ledger/integrity keeps reporting the mismatch. Reproduction: seed a user with balance_cc set directly (no ledger entry) -> POST /api/admin/ledger/backfill (mismatch cleared) -> update balance_cc to a new value -> POST backfill again -> response accounts_backfilled=1 but integrity still shows cached 450 / derived 300.
